title: Compliance-focused inference studio — customer workshop agenda & facilitation notes
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working facilitation guide for a 3-hour, compliance-focused inference studio with a regulated-customer (finance/healthcare). Goal: align on data residency and audit requirements, choose deployment mode (Private vs Dedicated), run a short latency/cost tradeoff exercise and surface a concrete POC acceptance checklist.

High-level goals for the session (shared with customer):
- Validate regulatory constraints (data flows, KMS/HSM, logging/audit retention)
- Map their workloads to Redwood deployment options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and identify blockers
- Prototype a serving profile: latency target, throughput, expected sequence lengths, cache hit assumptions
- Agree on POC success criteria and next steps (timelines, owners)

Attendees (approx):
- Customer: Head of Platform, Security Lead, ML Engineer, Product Owner
- Redwood: Aisha (SE lead), Marco (SRE/dedicated infra), Emily (product — private console), Ravi (solutions PM)

Agenda (3 hours) — timeboxed
00:00–00:10 (10m) — Welcome & alignment
- Quick intros (name + what they own)
- Goals for today's session (show 3 bullet goals)
- Success criteria: what signals would make this a go for POC

00:10–00:30 (20m) — Compliance intake (deep-dive)
- Customer walks through compliance doc (data residency, retention, encryption, audit windows, approved vendor list)
- Red flag callouts: any requirements that rule out Hosted (e.g., no third-party key access)
- Capture must-have vs nice-to-have

00:30–01:00 (30m) — Topology mapping + deployment recommendation exercise
- Present Redwood deployment matrix (one-slide cheat): Hosted / Dedicated / Private with tradeoffs
- Using their constraints, workshop recommended topology (draw live): network boundary, egress rules, KMS, bastion, audit log flow
- Output: recommended primary + fallback option (e.g., Private in customer VPC, Dedicated for test)

01:00–01:15 (15m) — Break

01:15–01:55 (40m) — Workload profiling & serving SLOs (interactive)
- Inputs: median/95th token length, average requests per minute, concurrency, SLA (p99 latency target)
- Exercise: attendees place sticky notes (digital) on a simple matrix: latency sensitivity vs cost-sensitivity
- Iterate: show how batching, KV caching, and quantization affect both latency & cost (quick heuristic table)
- Output: target model profile (model family/size, quantization preference, batching window)

01:55–02:30 (35m) — Mini-runbook: POC plan + demo script
- Walk through a minimum POC scope (what we will deploy, what data, what eval prompts)
- Demo script outline (if we do a short demo during POC): connectivity test, inference trace, audit log review, failover to fallback model
- Define test dataset: size (50–200 prompts), categories for regression checks, prompt sets to monitor hallucination risk

02:30–02:50 (20m) — Risks, mitigations, and commercial asks
- Identify top 5 risks (e.g., HSM onboarding time, network peering lag, data egress approvals)
- Mitigations & owners (draft timeline for each)
- Commercial note: estimated capacity needs and likely committed tier (if customer needs Dedicated) — rough numbers only

02:50–03:00 (10m) — Next steps & commitments
- Confirm owners, JIRA tasks, and target dates for POC kickoff
- Parking lot review, close

Slide outline (one-slide per bullet, recommended deck skeleton)
1) Title / objective slide — session title, date, attendees, success criteria
2) Current constraints summary — bullets from compliance intake (red/amber/green)
3) Redwood deployment options at-a-glance — simplified matrix + footnote on what each means operationally
4) Proposed topology diagram — VPC/peering, KMS, bastion, logging, private control plane if chosen
5) Workload profile & SLOs — table of expected QPS, concurrency, median/95th seq len, target latencies
6) Cost vs latency tradeoffs — visual: high-latency-low-cost vs low-latency-higher-cost with knobs (batching, quant, cache)
7) POC scope & demo script — step-by-step runbook for the 2–4 week POC
8) Test matrix & acceptance criteria — list of pass/fail checks for correctness, latency, reliability, security
9) Risks and timeline — owners and mitigation steps
10) Next steps & contact points — JIRA links, kickoff date options

Facilitation notes and prompts (try to keep interactive):
- Start with a short empathy statement: "we've run this with similar customers in regulated industries; common surprises are X & Y"
- When the customer reads compliance doc, ask: "what will take the longest internally to approve?" (aim to surface procurement/Legal blockers)
- For topology mapping, use a whiteboard; ask each customer stakeholder to annotate where they own the risk/approval
- Latency/cost sticky exercise: encourage tradeoffs — get them to pick a point on the matrix rather than saying "we want both"
- If the session stalls on legal minutiae, capture specifics in parking lot and pivot to topology/proofable engineering tasks

POC acceptance checklist (proposed) — pass conditions:
- Security: KMS/HSM integration verified, audit logs accessible for 90 days, role-based access control tested
- Network: VPC peering established, egress rules approved, subnets in allowed region
- Functional: 1,000 sample inferences with no crashes; p99 latency within agreed SLO on 4/5 runs
- Quality: baseline prompt set shows no regression (>95% match to golden outputs for templated responses)
- Observability: tracing hooks and cost breakdown enabled in Console; alerts for error rate >1%

Prep checklist for Redwood team (2 business days before session):
- Send pre-read: short compliance intake form + sample topology template
- Prepare one-page deck (slides 1–4) and a live whiteboard link
- Provision a sandbox Private/Dedicated plan (if demo needed) or a small Hosted demo model
- Confirm customer has single point-of-contact with authority for procurement questions

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Customer's preferred KMS vendor? HSM timelines unknown — set owner to Marco to confirm
- Need to validate whether audit logs retention 7 years is mandatory; will likely push to Private + long-term storage integration (S3 Glacier)
- Clarify whether synthetic data for POC is acceptable or if PII must be used in a masked form

Follow-ups (owners & tentative JIRA tickets)
- Marco: validate peering template + HSM onboarding time (JIRA-2107) — due 2026-02-18
- Emily: prepare Private control plane slide + console screenshots (PRD for Private demo) — JIRA-2181 — due 2026-02-16
- Aisha: assemble POC acceptance checklist into Confluence + send to customer — JIRA-2199 — due 2026-02-14

Quick facilitation tips (do/don't)
- DO use timeboxes visibly in the agenda; call out when 5 minutes remain
- DO capture decisions on the whiteboard and export a photo/PNG after the session
- DON'T try to resolve legal approvals in-session; capture the ask and route to Legal with clear owner
- DON'T overcommit on custom engineering in the POC; prefer config & topology work up-front

Appendix: short heuristics table (shareable, 1 slide)
- If p99 latency <300ms and QPS <50: suggest small-quantized model on Dedicated or Private with low batching
- If p99 latency can be soft (>=1s) and cost is main constraint: recommend batching + 8-bit quantization and possible Hosted option
- If data residency & KMS control required: default to Private (customer VPC) and plan HSM work in week 1

End of doc — notes: this is a working draft, use as facilitator script. Mark TODOs inline during the call and convert into JIRA tasks after session.
